question: What poverty rate did the State Bank of India project for India in 2024, as reported in June 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**4.6%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **State Bank of India (SBI)** Research report, specifically the **Ecowrap** edition, projected that India’s **poverty rate** for the year **2024** would reach **4.6%**.
 
• This projection, discussed in reports updated through **June 2025**, reflects a significant downward trend in the number of people living below the poverty line compared to previous decades.
 
• The report attributes this decline to a robust increase in **per capita income** and a significant shift in rural and urban consumption patterns as recorded in the **Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES)**.
 
• According to the **SBI** analysis, the reduction in poverty is a result of the government’s targeted **welfare schemes** and the **digitalization** of the economy, which has improved the efficiency of **Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT)**.
 
• The **4.6%** figure highlights the success of inclusive growth strategies that have moved a large segment of the **bottom of the pyramid** population into the **lower-middle-class** bracket.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **State Bank of India (SBI) Ecowrap:** 
 
 
• **Ecowrap** is a flagship economic research publication by **SBI**, led by the Group Chief Economic Adviser, **Dr. Soumya Kanti Ghosh**.
 
• It provides critical analysis on **macroeconomic indicators**, including **GDP growth**, inflation, and social development metrics.
 
 
 
• **Poverty Measurement in India:** 
 
 
• Historically, poverty in India was measured using the **Tendulkar Committee** and **Rangarajan Committee** methodologies based on **Monthly Per Capita Consumption Expenditure (MPCE)**.
 
• Recent estimates utilize the **Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES) 2022-23** data to provide a more contemporary view of poverty levels.
 
 
 
• **Government Interventions:** 
 
 
• Schemes like the **Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PM-GKAY)**, which provides free foodgrains to over **80 crore** people, have played a pivotal role in maintaining nutritional security and lowering poverty rates.
 
• The **Lakhpati Didi** initiative and **PM SVANidhi** are other examples of schemes aimed at economic empowerment of the marginalized sections.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:** 
 
 
• The **World Bank** defines **extreme poverty** as living on less than **$2.15 per day** (based on 2017 Purchasing Power Parity).
 
• India’s rapid reduction in poverty has been recognized by international organizations like the **UNDP**, noting that the country has successfully lifted millions out of **Multidimensional Poverty**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Rural vs. Urban Trends:** The **SBI** report noted that the decline in **rural poverty** has been more pronounced due to increased agricultural productivity and rural infrastructure development.
 
• **Income Inequality:** Along with the reduction in poverty, the report also highlighted a decline in **income inequality** (measured by the **Gini Coefficient**), suggesting that the benefits of economic growth are becoming more evenly distributed across different **decile groups**.
 
• **Data Validity:** The projection for **2024** (reported in **June 2025**) serves as a benchmark for evaluating the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDG)**, specifically **SDG 1**, which aims to end poverty in all its forms everywhere.

2f:T
